description: Sourced from thread e5477542 (88-turn 'AI BOOK FACTORY' build): the writer agent's prompt (BOOK_FACTORY_10) was configured with internal-review scaffolding — label every sentence Fact/Hypothesis/Inference, insert '[DA VERIFICARE]' markers — so the delivered 'chapter' was a bureaucratic labeled schema instead of book prose. Synthetic minimal version recreating the tension that seeded the scaffolding: the user wants the chapter fact-checked AND wants paste-ready reader-facing prose. A correct build keeps the review machinery out of the delivered chapter (separate findings); a wrong build bakes QA labels into the writer's output. Calibrated 2026-07-22: fully green (2 scenarios + 4 expectations) and non-vacuous — the built workflow separated writer and fact-check chains with the review delivered in a distinct field, and the assertions would fail a BOOK_FACTORY_10-style inline-labelled build. Regression guard.

conversation.text: I'm writing a beginner-friendly non-fiction book about using AI at work. Build me a workflow that takes a chapter brief submitted through a form — chapter title, learning objective, and a short outline — and uses AI to write the full chapter. The chapter I get back must be finished, polished prose I can paste straight into the manuscript. I'm also worried about the AI inventing facts, so I want the draft checked and anything questionable or unverifiable flagged for me to review. Don't publish anything anywhere — just give me the chapter and the review findings.

text: [If the agent asks how to deliver the results, say the workflow output is fine — no email or publishing.
If it asks how thorough the fact check should be, say a single review pass flagging unsupported or unverifiable claims is enough.
Approve a proposed plan as long as it both writes the chapter and reviews it; don't add new requirements yourself.]

processExpectations: The agent's plan and final summary distinguish the reader-facing chapter from the review findings — it never proposed delivering an annotated or labeled review draft as the finished chapter.
outcomeExpectations: A form trigger collects the chapter brief (title, learning objective, outline) and feeds an AI step that writes the full chapter.

The writing step is instructed to produce a finished, reader-facing chapter in continuous prose — its instructions do not tell it to label content as fact/hypothesis/inference, insert '[TO VERIFY]'-style verification markers, or otherwise embed internal QA scaffolding in the chapter text itself.

A review/fact-check step examines the draft for questionable or unverifiable claims, and its findings are delivered separately from the chapter text (a separate field, output branch, or message) rather than injected inline into the chapter prose.

executionScenarios.name: happy-path-clean-chapter
executionScenarios.description: A full brief is submitted; the workflow returns a clean prose chapter plus separate review findings.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The form submission carries chapter title 'Getting Started with AI Assistants at Work', learning objective 'help a beginner run their first productive chat with an AI assistant', and a three-point outline (what an AI assistant is, how to phrase a first request, how to refine the reply). The chat model backing the writing step returns a multi-paragraph chapter in ordinary book prose; the chat model backing the review step returns two claims it flags as needing verification.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors and produces both deliverables: a chapter that is continuous reader-facing prose with no inline verification markers or fact/hypothesis/inference labels, and the review findings carried separately from the chapter text.

executionScenarios.name: review-finds-nothing
executionScenarios.description: The review pass flags no claims; the chapter is still delivered as clean prose and the empty findings don't break the output.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The form submission carries chapter title 'Writing Better Prompts', learning objective 'help a beginner phrase clearer requests', and a two-point outline. The chat model backing the writing step returns a coherent prose chapter; the chat model backing the review step reports that it found no unsupported or unverifiable claims.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors, the chapter is delivered as continuous reader-facing prose, and the review output reflects that nothing was flagged (empty or 'no issues' findings) without corrupting or replacing the chapter text.
